findings.description: At 09:00 four cups are clearly on the felt (two front, one rear, one partially behind on the left). By 09:50 and 09:75 only three cups remain. Neither hand picks up or moves a cup; one hand is holding a coin above the cups and the other rests on the felt. A cup disappears for no reason.

From 00:00 to 02:50 the middle cup is filled to the brim with a stack of gold embossed coins. At 02:75 the top coin turns silver-faced, and after about 04:30 the stack is no longer visible. No coin is removed or added to this cup.

The four cups start in a triangular cluster with clear gaps (00:00-03:00). By 05:00-06:00 they stand in a straight, evenly spaced row across the felt. The hands only rest on the end cups and never slide them into a line, so the rearrangement is not explained by the action or by the camera move.

During 00:00-05:00 several spectators stand and sit close behind the table. As the continuous shot pulls back (07:00-09:75), the room behind the performer is nearly empty: rows of vacant chairs and only one or two dim figures. Spectators vanish with no cut.

Early frames show a very large table with a detailed white ornamental border, dense rings of large decorated chips, and three big gold coins on the central felt. In the later wide frames the table is a smaller round table with plain red cloth, one thin chain-pattern ring of small discs, and a mostly empty center. These changes go beyond what the change in perspective can explain.
